title: The Bell in the Marsh
author: Claude, 04/10/2026, in the werewolf's spirit: a branching tale whose turn is taken in a scene (left or right on the causeway)

stages.journal: {giver} has asked you to find out what rings the bell in the marsh by {village}.
stages.canvas: The lord raises it with a tired face. He does not believe in drowned ghosts, but two of his men went out to look and did not come back, and the village will not sleep.
facts: A bell rings at night in the marsh by {village}, where an old chapel sank long ago.
The villagers say the drowned dead ring it.
Two men of {village} went out to look a fortnight ago and have not come back.

{giver}: Your people at {village} say the drowned chapel's bell rings at night in the marsh. Two men went to look and never came back.
You do not believe in ghosts, but you cannot explain the two missing men.

stages.journal: Ask the people of {village} about the bell.
stages.canvas: The villagers lower their voices. Everyone has heard the bell; nobody has gone near it since the two men vanished.
facts: The bell rings only on still, foggy nights.
The two missing men were brothers-in-law, Oswin and Tam.
An old causeway runs into the marsh toward the drowned chapel; it forks halfway.

locals_of:{village}: You believe the drowned dead of the old chapel ring the bell; your grandmother said they call the living to join them.
Oswin and Tam went down the old causeway to look a fortnight ago and never came back.
The causeway forks halfway: left toward the drowned chapel, right toward the reed beds where nobody goes.

stages.journal: Wait for a still, foggy night by the marsh of {village}.

locals_of:{village}: You believe the drowned dead ring the bell. The lord's champion waits for a foggy night to go and see; you pray they come back.
Oswin and Tam went down the old causeway a fortnight ago and never came back.

stages.journal: The bell is ringing in the marsh.

scene.title: The marsh by {village}

opening.canvas: A still night, thick with fog. Somewhere ahead in the marsh, a bell tolls, slow and cracked. The old causeway runs out into the reeds and, a little way on, forks. End by asking what the player does.
facts: The bell is somewhere to the left, toward the drowned chapel.
The causeway forks: left toward the bell, right into the reed beds.

findings.text: A new hemp rope tied to a causeway post, leading off to the left toward the bell: no ghost ties rope.
A man's boot stuck in the mud at the start of the right fork, and fresh footprints going into the reeds.

hazards.trigger: stepping off the causeway into the marsh

scene.closing: The bell falls silent behind you.

choices.label: Follow the causeway left, toward the bell
Take the right fork, where the footprints go
Go back to the village and wait for another night

stages.journal: Follow the bell to the drowned chapel.

scene.title: The drowned chapel

opening.canvas: The causeway ends at the broken tower of the drowned chapel, half sunk in black water. The bell hangs in the tower; a rope runs from it down into the dark. Lantern light shows through a gap in the wall. End by asking what the player does.
facts: Someone is inside the tower; there is lantern light and the smell of tar.
The bell rope has been pulled recently: it still sways.

findings.text: Crates of salt and wine stacked inside the tower, with no toll paid on any of them: smugglers land here, and ring the bell to keep the village away.

encounters.name: Oswin of {village}
encounters.persona: one of the two missing men, bound and gagged in a corner, thin and terrified
knows: The smugglers caught him and Tam on the causeway; they keep him to work, and they killed no one.
Tam broke free on the first night and ran into the reed beds; Oswin does not know if he lived.

hazards.trigger: being seen or heard by the smuggler keeping watch at the tower

scene.closing: Whatever the player did, they leave the chapel knowing smugglers ring the bell to keep the village away.

stages.journal: Follow the footprints into the reed beds.

scene.title: The reed beds

opening.canvas: The footprints wind deep into the reeds, to a hut of woven rushes on a hummock of dry ground. A man is hiding inside, starved and wild-eyed. End by asking what the player does.
facts: The hut is tiny and hidden; someone has lived here for days.
The man inside is barefoot: the boot on the causeway was his.

findings.text: The man is Tam, one of the two missing: men with lanterns caught him and Oswin at the chapel, and he escaped into the reeds and has hidden here since, too afraid to cross the causeway.

encounters.name: Tam of {village}
encounters.persona: a villager hiding in the reeds for a fortnight, starved, frightened of the lantern men
knows: Men with lanterns, not ghosts, ring the bell; they took Oswin and he ran.
He does not know what became of Oswin.

scene.closing: Whatever the player did, they leave the reeds with Tam's word: men, not ghosts, ring the bell.

stages.journal: Tell {giver} what you found in the marsh.

{giver}: You sent the player into the marsh after the bell, and you wait for news of your two missing men.
locals_of:{village}: The lord's champion came back from the marsh. You do not yet know what they found.

choices.label: Tell {giver} of the smugglers in the chapel
choices.canvas: The lord hears it, and his tired face hardens: smugglers on his own marsh, using his people's fear. He thanks the player plainly.

{giver}: The player has just told you smugglers land at the drowned chapel and ring the bell to keep your village away.

{giver}.text: They found Oswin alive, held by the smugglers.

choices.label: Tell {giver} what Tam saw
choices.canvas: The lord is glad of one man found alive, and troubled by what he says: men, not ghosts, on his marsh.

{giver}: The player has just told you that Tam of {village} lives: he hid in the reed beds, and says men with lanterns, not ghosts, ring the bell.
You do not yet know who those men are.

unmasked.memory: The player found that smugglers ring the bell in the marsh by {village}, not the drowned dead.
unmasked.journal: The bell in the marsh will ring no more.

consequences.summary: The ghost bell of {village} was rung by smugglers landing at the drowned chapel.

consequences.text: It was smugglers ringing the bell all along, not the drowned dead.
Oswin came home from the drowned chapel, alive.

survivor.memory: The player brought back word of Tam from the marsh by {village}: men, not ghosts, ring that bell.
survivor.journal: Tam is home; the bell still rings.

consequences.text: Tam came back from the reed beds and swears men with lanterns ring the bell.

failure.memory: I asked the player to look into the bell of {village}, and nothing came of it.
failure.journal: The bell still rings in the marsh.
